subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class core browser-plugin config for per-agent/subagent browser profile binding plus per-profile proxy settings, or keep this as external/CDP/plugin orchestration for now?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the implementation would define new config, proxy credentials, egress routing, and browser state ownership boundaries that require product and security intent before code work.

options.title: Design the core browser contract
options.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for per-profile proxy, SecretRef handling, agent inheritance, concurrency limits, diagnostics, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Split into narrower tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella while proxy transport policy and subagent browser ownership proceed through separate maintainer-owned issues.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document Remote CDP, Browserless-style infrastructure, or ClawHub/plugin wrappers as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide not to add core config.

recommendation.title: Design the core browser contract
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for per-profile proxy, SecretRef handling, agent inheritance, concurrency limits, diagnostics, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from recent browser profile, extension-driver, docs, and security-boundary history.
